subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS Gateway LaunchAgents include documented Nix/user-bin directories in the generated service PATH, expose an explicit operator opt-in, or keep the canonical minimal PATH and update docs accordingly?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally harden macOS service PATHs, but the Nix docs and prior fixed issue history promise macOS launchd Nix discovery; automation should not choose that command-resolution trust boundary or new config surface.

options.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the hardened macOS default while adding a documented operator-controlled service PATH option only if schema, doctor, docs, and security tests make the trust choice explicit.

options.title: Restore documented Nix support by default
options.body: Include Nix profile paths on macOS as the docs already promise, with focused tests and an explicit security rationale for why Nix is acceptable while other user package-manager paths remain excluded.

options.title: Keep hardened policy and correct docs
options.body: Leave macOS LaunchAgent PATH minimal, update the Nix docs to remove the macOS promise, and point users to supported exec-level or system-install paths.

recommendation.title: Keep default minimal, add explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Preserve the hardened macOS default while adding a documented operator-controlled service PATH option only if schema, doctor, docs, and security tests make the trust choice explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest recent decision signal on adjacent managed service PATH precedence and hardening tradeoffs.
